2895-following-the-equator-a-journey-aro.title: A Journey Around The World
2895-following-the-equator-a-journey-aro.creator: Mark Twain
2895-following-the-equator-a-journey-aro.description: A book by Mark Twain. a Birthday CHAPTER V. A lesson in Pronunciation—Reverence for Robert Burns—The Southern Cross—Troublesome Constellations—Victoria for a Name—Islands on the Map—Alofa and Fortuna—Recruiting for the Queensland Plantations —Captain Warren's NoteBook—Recruiting not thoroughly Popular CHAPTER VI. Missionaries Obstruct Business—The Sugar Planter and the Kanaka—The Planter's View—Civilizing the Kanaka—The Missionary's View—The Result —Repentant Kanakas—Wrinkles—The Death Rate in Queensland CHAPTER VII.

33642-earth-alert.creator: Unknown
33642-earth-alert.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Two days later she walked down to the bank and instructed the teller to transfer $5,000 of her money to a checking account in her name at the Security First National Bank in Los Angeles.

arxiv-2111-01422.title: Maximum Length-Constrained Flows and Disjoint Paths: Distributed, Deterministic and Fast
arxiv-2111-01422.creator: Bernhard Haeupler D Ellis Hershkowitz Thatchaphol Saranurak Carnegie Mellon University & Carnegie Mellon University & University of Michigan ETH Zürich ETH Zürich haeupler@cs.cmu.edu dhershko@cs.cmu.edu thsa@umich.edu
arxiv-2111-01422.description: Abstract Computing routing schemes that support both high throughput and low latency is one of the core challenges of network optimization. Such routes can be formalized as h h -length flows which are defined as flows whose flow paths have length at most h h .

arxiv-2112-01106.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Manuel B. Branco, Isabel Colaço, Ignacio Ojeda. In this paper, we introduce and study the numerical semigroups generated by { a 1 , a 2 , … } ⊂ ℕ \{a_{1},a_{2},\ldots\}\subset\mathbb{N} such that a 1 a_{1} is the repunit number in base b > 1 b>1 of length n > 1 n>1 and a i − a i − 1 = a ​ b i − 2 , a_{i}-a_{i-1}=a\,b^{i-2}, for every i ≥ 2 i\geq 2 , where a a is a positive integer

arxiv-2202-07096.title: Learning to Discover Medicines
arxiv-2202-07096.creator: Minh-Tri Nguyen, Thin Nguyen, Truyen Tran
arxiv-2202-07096.description: Abstract Discovering new medicines is the hallmark of human endeavor to live a better and longer life. Yet the pace of discovery has slowed down as we need to venture into more wildly unexplored biomedical space to find one that matches today’s high standard.

arxiv-2303-02381.title: Effects of intrinsic decoherence on discord-like correlation measures of two-qubit spin squeezing model
arxiv-2303-02381.creator: Venkat Abhignan, R. Muthuganesan
arxiv-2303-02381.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Venkat Abhignan, R. Muthuganesan. Abstract Quantum decoherence happens when the system interacts with the environment. Quantum correlation behaviours in the two-qubit spin squeezing model are studied under the influence of intrinsic decoherence. Quantitative results were determined, which depend on parameters of the physical system by checking different quantifiers of quantum correlation such as entanglement, local quantum uncertainty, trace distance discord and uncertainty-induced quantum nonlocality.

arxiv-2405-08049.title: Optimizing Synthetic Correlated Diffusion Imaging for Breast Cancer Tumour Delineation
arxiv-2405-08049.creator: Chi-en Amy Tai, Alexander Wong
arxiv-2405-08049.description: Abstract Breast cancer is a significant cause of death from cancer in women globally, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic imaging to enhance patient outcomes. Accurate tumour identification is essential for diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring, emphasizing the importance of advanced imaging technologies that provide detailed views of tumour characteristics and disease.

arxiv-2405-10813.title: Tidal Love Numbers from EFT of Black Hole Perturbations with Timelike Scalar Profile
arxiv-2405-10813.creator: Chams Gharib Ali Barura
arxiv-2405-10813.description: Abstract We study static tidal Love numbers (TLNs) of a static and spherically symmetric black hole for odd-parity metric perturbations. We describe black hole perturbations using the effective field theory (EFT), formulated on an arbitrary background with a timelike scalar profile in the context of scalar-tensor theories.

arxiv-2406-18511.title: High-Speed Combinatorial Polymerization Through Kinetic-Trap Encoding
arxiv-2406-18511.creator: Félix Benoist, Pablo Sartori
arxiv-2406-18511.description: Abstract Like the letters in the alphabet forming words, reusing components of a heterogeneous mixture is an efficient strategy for assembling a large number of target structures. Examples range from synthetic DNA origami to proteins self-assembling into complexes. The standard self-assembly paradigm views target structures as free-energy minima of a mixture.

arxiv-2408-11033.title: An FUV-detected Accretion Shock at the Star-Disk Boundary of FU Ori
arxiv-2408-11033.creator: Adolfo S. Carvalho, Lynne A. Hillenbrand, Kevin France, Gregory J. Herczeg
arxiv-2408-11033.description: Abstract FU Ori objects are the most extreme eruptive young stars known. Their 4 to 5 magnitude photometric outbursts last for decades and are attributed to a factor of up to 10,000 increase in the stellar accretion rate. The nature of the accretion disk-to-star interface in FU Ori objects has remained a mystery for decades.

arxiv-2506-09141.title: Unification of Exceptional Points and Transmission Peak Degeneracies in a Highly Tunable Magnon-Photon Dimer
arxiv-2506-09141.creator: Alexander S. Carney, Juan S. Salcedo-Gallo, Salil K. Bedkihal, Mattias Fitzpatrick
arxiv-2506-09141.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexander S. Carney, Juan S. Salcedo-Gallo, Salil K. Bedkihal, Mattias Fitzpatrick. Exceptional points (EPs), spectral singularities arising in non-Hermitian dynamical systems, have drawn widespread attention for their potential to enhance sensor capability by leveraging characteristic square-root frequency splitting. However, the advantages of EP sensors have remained highly contested, primarily due to their inherent hypersensitivity to model errors and loss of precision arising from eigenbasis collapse, quantified by the Petermann noise factor.

arxiv-2508-08526.title: Playing Atari Space Invaders with Sparse Cosine Optimized Policy Evolution
arxiv-2508-08526.creator: Jim O’Connor, Jay B. Nash, Derin Gezgin, Gary B. Parker
arxiv-2508-08526.description: Abstract Evolutionary approaches have previously been shown to be effective learning methods for a diverse set of domains. However, the domain of game-playing poses a particular challenge for evolutionary methods due to the inherently large state space of video games.

arxiv-2511-00977.title: Modeling Microenvironment Trajectories on Spatial Transcriptomics with NicheFlow
arxiv-2511-00977.creator: Kristiyan Sakalyan, Alessandro Palma, Filippo Guerranti, Fabian J. Theis, Stephan Günnemann
arxiv-2511-00977.description: Abstract Understanding the evolution of cellular microenvironments in spatiotemporal data is essential for deciphering tissue development and disease progression. While experimental techniques like spatial transcriptomics now enable high-resolution mapping of tissue organization across space and time, current methods that model cellular evolution operate at the single-cell level, overlooking the coordinated development of cellular states in a tissue.

pmc-10509541.title: Correction: Non-peptide compounds from Kronopolites svenhedini (Verhoeff) and their antitumor and iNOS inhibitory activities
pmc-10509541.creator: Yuan-Nan Yuan, Jin-Qiang Li, Hong-Bin Fang, Shao-Jun Xing, Yong-Ming Yan, Yong-Xian Cheng, Jeroen S Dickschat
pmc-10509541.description: d finally determined the correct structure as shown in Figure 1. The revised structure of 1 is supported by the HMBC correlations of H-2/C-1, C-3, C-4, C-8a, H-4/C-3, C-4a, C-5, C-8a, C-9, H-5/C-4, C-4a, C-6, C-7, C-8a, H-9/C-2, C-3, C-4, H-10/C-7, C-8, C-8a, H-11/C-6, and H-12/C-7. pmc-10625128.title: Biocompatible Cryogel with Good Breathability, Exudate Management, Antibacterial and Immunomodulatory Properties for Infected Diabetic Wound Healing
pmc-10625128.creator: Yang Li, Zifeng Yang, Qi Sun, Ruijun Xu, Renjie Li, Dingcai Wu, Rongkang Huang, Feng Wang, Yong Li
pmc-10625128.description: Due to the complex microenvironment and healing process of diabetic wounds, developing wound dressing with good biocompatibility, mechanical stability, breathability, exudate management, antibacterial ability, and immunomodulatory property is highly desired but remains a huge challenge. Herein, a multifunctional cryogel is designed and prepared with bio‐friendly bacterial cellulose, gelatin, and dopamine under the condition of sodium periodate oxidation.

pmc-11472260.title: Engineering Triphasic Nanocomposite Coatings on Pretreated Mg Substrates for Biomedical Applications
pmc-11472260.creator: Xijuan Chai, Jiajia Lin, Changlu Xu, Dongwei Sun, Huinan Hannah Liu
pmc-11472260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Biodegradable polymer-based nanocomposite coatings provide multiple advantages to modulate the corrosion resistance and cytocompatibility of magnesium (Mg) alloys for biomedical applications. Biodegradable poly(glycerol sebacate) (PGS) is a promising candidate used for medical implant applications.

pmc-11491731.title: Lipid peroxidation triggered by the degradation of xCT contributes to gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis in COPD
pmc-11491731.creator: Tianhua Hou, Laiyu Zhu, Yan Zhang, Ying Tang, Yun Gao, Shucheng Hua, Xinxin Ci, Liping Peng
pmc-11491731.description: BackgroundPyroptosis is an inflammatory form of regulated necrosis that has been implicated in the pathogenesis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the role of lipid peroxidation in pyroptosis and its underlying mechanisms in COPD remain unclear.MethodsIn vitro, human bronchial epithelial cells (Beas-2b cells) were exposed to cigarette smoke extract (CSE) for 24 h.

pmc-11545557.title: Effect of High-Tannin and -Polyphenol Plant Material Supplement on Rumen Fermentation, Nitrogen Partitioning and Nutrient Utilization in Beef Cattle
pmc-11545557.creator: Pichad Khejornsart, Theerayut Juntanam, Pongsatorn Gunun, Nirawan Gunun, Anusorn Cherdthong, Alejandro Plascencia, Richard Avery Zinn
pmc-11545557.description: Simple SummaryIt may be possible to manipulate rumen fermentation and decrease enteric methane by adding tannin-containing plants to ruminant diet. The effect of tannin-rich tree foliage addition in diets on feed utilization and rumen fermentation characteristics in beef cattle was thus evaluated. This study suggests that feeding 10 g/d of added Anacardium occidentale L. or Careya arborea Roxb.

pmc-11633500.title: Extracellular Vesicles Derived from Ligament Tissue Transport Interleukin‐17A to Mediate Ligament‐To‐Bone Crosstalk in Ankylosing Spondylitis
pmc-11633500.creator: Kaiyang Wang, Jingshun Lu, Chenyu Song, Mu Qiao, Yao Li, Menghan Chang, Hongda Bao, Yong Qiu, Bang‐Ping Qian
pmc-11633500.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Pathological new bone formation is a critical feature of the progression of ankylosing spondylitis (AS), and spine ankylosis is a distinctive feature of this condition. Ligaments are the primary regions of pathological new bone formation in AS. Here, it is demonstrated that ligament tissue‐derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their interleukin‐17A (IL‐17A) cargo mediate the communication between the tissue and other cells. The investigation revealed that IL‐17A in EVs can activate the JAK‐STAT3 pathway, thereby stimulating the expression of MMP14 in AS ligament.

pmc-11654697.title: AI-driven universal lower-limb exoskeleton system for community ambulation
pmc-11654697.creator: Dawit Lee, Sanghyub Lee, Aaron J. Young
pmc-11654697.description: Exoskeletons offer promising solutions for improving human mobility, but a key challenge is ensuring the controller adapts to changing walking conditions. We present an artificial intelligence (AI)–driven universal exoskeleton system that dynamically switches assistance types between walking modes, modulates assistance levels corresponding to the ground slope, and delivers assistance timely based on the current gait phase in real-time.

pmc-12422802.title: Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness During the 2023/2024 Season: A Test‐Negative Case–Control Study Among Emergency Hospital Admissions With Respiratory Conditions in Northern Ireland
pmc-12422802.creator: Magda Bucholc, Mark G. O'Doherty, Declan T. Bradley
pmc-12422802.description: BackgroundWe evaluated the effectiveness of the influenza vaccine programme against infection among emergency hospital admissions with respiratory conditions in Northern Ireland during the 2023/2024 influenza season.MethodsUsing a test‐negative design, we compared the odds of vaccination between patients who tested positive (cases) and negative (controls) for laboratory‐confirmed influenza, adjusting for confounders.

pmc-12439565.title: Verification of tetanus vaccination status of children admitted for animal bites in a pediatric emergency department
pmc-12439565.creator: Mathilde Nibbio, Claire de Jorna, Marion Lagrée, Diariatou Diallo, Constance Leruste, Melany Liber, François Dubos
pmc-12439565.description: Animal bites are high-risk wounds for tetanus. Our objective was to verify that children admitted to the pediatric emergency department (PED) for bites had reliable management of the risk of tetanus. This retrospective descriptive study was conducted at Lille University Hospital between 2015 and 2020.

pmc-12572084.title: Contrast analysis for competing hypotheses: A tutorial using the R package cofad
pmc-12572084.creator: Mirka Henninger, Simone Malejka, Johannes Titz
pmc-12572084.description: Researchers in psychology traditionally use analysis of variance to examine differences between multiple groups or conditions. A less well-known, but valuable alternative is contrast analysis — a simple statistical method for testing directional, theoretically motivated hypotheses that are defined prior to data collection.

pmc-13409628.title: Parotid Metastases from Head–Neck Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prognostic Stratification
pmc-13409628.creator: Giulia Togo, Luca Calabrese, Giovanni dell’Aversana Orabona, Franco Ionna, Francesco Longo, Renato de Falco, Pietro Perotti, Ottavio Piccin, Luca Gazzini
pmc-13409628.description: Simple SummaryCutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck frequently metastasizes to regional lymph nodes. However, the relative prognostic impact of metastases involving the parotid gland compared with those affecting the lateral cervical lymphatic basin remains a matter of debate.

pmc-13420535.title: Characterizing highly conserved fragments in 3′UTRs via statistical and transfer learning approaches
pmc-13420535.creator: Eric S Ho, Ash Baeck-Hubloux, Nathan Dinh, Ava Severino, Ciara Troy
pmc-13420535.description: 3′ Untranslated regions (3′UTRs) serve as regulatory platforms that modulate steps in the central dogma through the binding of RNA-binding proteins and miRNAs. Their binding sites are often identified through orthologous regions among species. A separate but related discovery was the ultraconserved elements (UCEs) detected in human, rat, and mouse genomes two decades ago.

pmc-13539909.title: Age at Menarche, Cardiometabolic Disease Prevalence, and Disease Control in Korean Women: Analysis of the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
pmc-13539909.creator: Yuki Gen, Gyu-Na Lee, Kyung-Do Han, Yun Sung Jo
pmc-13539909.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEarly menarche is linked to adverse cardiometabolic outcomes, but its relationship with disease management remains unclear. We examined associations between menarcheal age and the prevalence and control of cardiometabolic diseases in Korean women.MethodsIn 25,227 women aged ≥19 years from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES), 2014-2023, menarcheal age was categorized as early (<12 years), intermediate (12-15 years; reference), and late (≥16 years).

pmc-13605172.title: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life in Pediatric Subjects with Molar Incisor Hypomineralization: An Umbrella Review of Domain-Specific Impact and Treatment-Related Changes
pmc-13605172.creator: Massimo Pisano, Giuseppe Sangiovanni, Eugenio Frucci, Michela Scorziello, María del Carmen Villanueva-Vilchis, Giuseppina De Benedetto
pmc-13605172.description: Highlights What are the main findings? The present umbrella review synthesized six systematic reviews, showing an overall child self-reported OHRQoL percentage impact index of 21.76% in pediatric subjects with MIH, with the highest domain-specific impact across both child and parents/caregivers observed in the oral domain (26.43%), followed by the psychological (20.25%), functional (19.50%), and social (11.75%) domains.
